A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ContraBin study. All 17 pages of v4 and 27 pages of v5 are readable, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither contains a separate appendix. The substantial reformatting does not prevent reliable content matching.

before.justification: v4 reports original binary-code benchmark results, ablations, embedding analyses, and case studies in Sections 4-5, including Tables 3-8.

after.justification: v5 retains the work's original quantitative experiments, ablations, embedding visualizations, and case studies in Sections 4-5.

M1.justification: The anchored source/comment encoder, trainable binary encoder, primary contrastive learning, simplex interpolation, intermediate contrastive loss, and downstream fine-tuning remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the CodeT5 adaptation retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use AnghaBench for pretraining and evaluate POJ-104 functionality classification, function-name recovery, and AnghaBench summarization and reverse engineering. DIRT becomes DIRE in Section 3.2, but the dataset construction and Table 2 counts remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 3-6 retain RoBERTa, CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, and ContraBin-PCL comparisons. Table 8 retains T5 and CodeT5. No comparator is added or removed from the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, training budgets, sequence lengths, batch sizes, and metrics remain unchanged. v5 newly documents shared fine-tuning controls; it does not establish a changed evaluation design. GLUE-to-GLEU is a naming correction. Seed-reporting changes are assessed under E5.

E4.justification: Both retain the comment, anchor, and interpolation ablations; human-versus-generated comment analysis; multi-step versus multi-objective comparison; and positive and negative case studies. Revised captions describe existing analyses.

E5.justification: v5 Section 4.1 newly asserts that all downstream experiments use seed 123456. This conflicts with the seed-42 settings for summarization and reverse engineering retained in Section 3.2. Seed reporting therefore changes, but actual seed changes or reruns are not established. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 3-8 retain identical numerical entries and rankings, including ContraBin's POJ-104 MAP of 43.78 and summarization BLEU-4 of 34.36. The embedding plots, case-study outputs, and reported multi-objective performance collapse are also retained.

T1.justification: The manifold assumptions, embedding definitions, interpolation equations, and contrastive and fine-tuning losses in Sections 2.1-2.3 are mathematically unchanged. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: Section 1 refocuses the priority claim on being the first contrastive framework for LLVM IR representations and consolidates the intermediate-learning contribution into the two-stage framework. The broad binary-analysis claims, four downstream tasks, and comment-quality finding remain.

C2.justification: v5 Section 4.1 adds an explicit argument that matched fine-tuning controls allow performance differences to be attributed primarily to embedding quality. The existing explanations of comment noise and limitations concerning preservation of code structure remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 newly specifies AdamW and shared fine-tuning and early-stopping controls, and identifies Figure 6 as t-SNE. The Zenodo record changes from 14435423 to 15219264, and the introduction explicitly reports pre-trained model availability. Code and dataset availability were already reported in v4.

R1.justification: Section 1 changes the novelty positioning from first intermediate contrastive learning for binary analysis to first contrastive representation learning for LLVM IR. The cited works and Section 6 discussion remain unchanged; the switch to author-year citations is bibliographic reformatting.

P1.justification: The introduction's motivation, evaluation overview, and contribution list are rewritten, with six contributions consolidated into four. Terminology, typos, authorship, affiliations, and publication headers are updated. The section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a two-column IEEE layout to a single-column TMLR layout, resizing and relocating figures, tables, and the algorithm. All ten figures and eight tables are retained. Figure 6 and Table 7 receive expanded captions, and Table 7 gains clearer ablation labels.

improvement.justification: v5 clarifies the LLVM-specific novelty, comparison controls, figure/table descriptions, and reported resource access. However, its new universal seed-123456 assertion conflicts with retained seed-42 settings in Section 3.2, introducing reproducibility ambiguity. With the scientific results unchanged, the PDFs do not establish whether these limited clarity gains outweigh the new inconsistency.
